# Contributing to PhoneDrop

Thanks for helping. PhoneDrop is small on purpose: one tray exe, no iPhone app, nothing running
when nothing is happening. Contributions that keep it that way are very welcome.

**Where to start:** issues labelled
[good first issue](https://github.com/mynameishaheer/phonedrop/labels/good%20first%20issue) are
scoped to a few hours. Comment on one so nobody doubles up. For anything bigger, open an issue or
a [Discussion](https://github.com/mynameishaheer/phonedrop/discussions) before writing code.
Ideas that are already planned live in [docs/ROADMAP.md](docs/ROADMAP.md).

**Security bugs do not go in issues.** Follow [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md) and report them
privately.

By taking part you agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md).

## Building and testing

You need Go 1.24 or newer on any OS. You do not need Windows to work on most of the code.

```sh
scripts/build.sh              # go test ./..., then cross-compiles phonedrop.exe
go test -race ./...           # what CI runs
GOOS=windows go vet .         # vets the Windows-only files from Linux or macOS
gofmt -l .                    # must print nothing
```

Files ending `_windows.go` only build for Windows; everything else is portable and is tested on
Linux in CI. Keep logic that doesn't need Win32 in the portable files so it can be unit-tested.
The code map is in [docs/DEV.md](docs/DEV.md) and the wire protocol, which is the contract
between the PC and the shortcuts, is in [docs/PROTOCOL.md](docs/PROTOCOL.md).

## The rules

1. **Standard library only, no cgo.** No third-party Go modules. Windows APIs are called through
   `syscall`. This keeps the exe small and the supply chain empty. (The one external tool,
   `go-winres`, is run by hand to regenerate the icon and version resource, see `scripts/build.sh`.)
2. **Idle must cost nothing.** No polling loops, no tickers while the panel is hidden, no
   background timers. Block on accepts and channels; check expiry lazily when state is touched.
3. **Stream, don't buffer.** Received files go to disk as they arrive.
4. **Never log secrets, signatures, file names or text contents.** The log is something users
   paste into issues.
5. **Protocol changes need a spec change.** Update `docs/PROTOCOL.md` (and the shortcuts guide
   and generator, if the phone side changes) in the same pull request.
6. Match the surrounding style: `gofmt`, short comments that say *why*, compact code.

## Previewing the UI

`phonedrop.exe -preview <folder>` renders every panel state (ready, paused, pairing, recent list,
outbox and so on) to PNG files without opening any window, so you can check layout changes
without clicking through the app. It works on real Windows and under Wine, which is enough for
layout and spacing; colours and fonts only look right on real Windows. Please attach the
before and after PNGs to pull requests that touch the UI.

## The iPhone shortcuts

The shortcuts are written by hand in [docs/SHORTCUTS.md](docs/SHORTCUTS.md), and the same six
are generated by [shortcuts/build.py](shortcuts/build.py) (Python 3, standard library only):

```sh
python3 -I shortcuts/build.py          # writes shortcuts/unsigned/*.shortcut and validates them
python3 -I shortcuts/build.py --check  # validates only
```

The generator checks that every file parses, every If/Repeat is closed and every variable is set
before use. Output is deterministic, so a rebuild without changes gives identical files, and
reviewers can see exactly what changed. Apple only imports **signed** shortcuts and signing
needs a Mac (`shortcuts/sign-all.sh`), so if you change the generator, say in the pull request
whether you were able to sign and run the result on an iPhone. Keep the guide and the
generator in step: they describe the same shortcuts.

## Commits and pull requests

- One logical change per commit. Subject line in the imperative, about 70 characters, with an
  optional area prefix, as in the existing history: `Shortcuts: store If comparison values as
  text tokens`, `Log why a request was refused`. Explain *why* in the body when it isn't obvious.
- Add or update tests for behaviour changes. Tests for the portable code run on every push.
- Before opening a pull request: `gofmt -l .` is empty, `GOOS=windows go vet .` and
  `go test -race ./...` pass, and docs are updated. The pull request template has the checklist.
- Windows-only changes: say which Windows version you tried them on.
- New user-visible behaviour gets a line under `[Unreleased]` in [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md).
